subject: Operator access & custody carveouts for ValleyHealth on-prem deployment
messages:
From: Katie Lin <katie@valleyhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@valleyhealth.com>, contracts@bakerco.com
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operator access and evidence window for on-prem deployment

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prepare the MSA/Order Form addendum for the on-prem deployment (ValleyHealth site A), our security and procurement teams asked for two clarified items that we want to capture in Exhibit G before we proceed: 

1) Operator access carveout: we need explicit language limiting Redwood personnel console/SSH access to a witnessed, time-boxed window for incident response only, with a requirement for local ValleyHealth observer and audit log export within 24 hours of the session end.

2) Evidence & escrow-like snapshot: ValleyHealth is not asking for a software escrow deposit, but we need a defined snapshot-and-witness workflow that allows ValleyHealth to request a read-only forensic snapshot of the deployed model runtime and init configuration under a lawful business continuity event. The ask includes a maximum turnaround (30 days) and a chain-of-custody manifest.

Attached is our proposed high-level language from legal and a short evidence matrix. Can Redwood confirm whether these map to any existing Exhibits or if you prefer to add an addendum? If you can share draft wording by EOD Friday, that helps our procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Katie
Katie Lin
Sr. Manager, IT Security
ValleyHealth
Attachment: evidence_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx)
Attachment: ValleyHealth_requested_clauses.pdf (pdf)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Katie Lin <katie@valleyhealth.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@valleyhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator access and evidence window for on-prem deployment

Hi Katie — thanks for the clear note and the matrix. We can accommodate the spirit of both asks; a few quick points and next steps: 

- Operator access: Redwood supports time-boxed, witnessed sessions. We typically implement an access request / justification + ValleyHealth observer requirement, session recording when permitted, and a signed attestation post-session. We will propose specific language that ties to the Order Form incident response SLA and includes the 24-hour audit export requirement.

- Snapshot/workflow: We do not offer escrow deposits by default, but we have an operational snapshot and witness playbook we can attach as an Exhibit (read-only evidence export + checksum manifest). We need to confirm retention and what components are included (runtime binaries vs config vs telemetry).

I'm looping in Alex (legal lead) and Lauren (deploy operations) to draft a concise Exhibit G redline. Alex / Lauren — can you suggest guarded wording that balances ValleyHealth's request for a 30-day maximum turnaround and our need to limit what constitutes a requestable "forensic snapshot" (e.g., exclude ephemeral telemetry and third-party model artifacts)? 

Goal: 1) Draft Exhibit G redline attached; 2) Short operations annex describing the witnessed session steps and evidence handoff; 3) Return to ValleyHealth by EOD Friday (6/23).

- Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference
Attachment: ValleyHealth_MSA_exhibit_G_draft.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Katie Lin <katie@valleyhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@valleyhealth.com>, contracts@bakerco.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator access and evidence window for on-prem deployment

Hi all — sharing proposed redline and short notes below. Attaching a redline doc with bracketed language (redline_msa_valleyhealth.docx). Key points: 

1) Definition clarity: define "Forensic Snapshot" narrowly as a point-in-time read-only export of configuration files, packaged runtime artifacts owned by the customer or Redwood-verified open models, and a cryptographic manifest. Explicitly exclude ephemeral telemetry (real-time request logs) and third-party licensed model weights unless the customer has separate rights.

2) Turnaround: 30 calendar days for non-emergency requests; 7 calendar days for incidents declared under the incident response SLA. We propose acceptance testing windows for the snapshot handoff and a mutually agreed witness schedule.

3) Access: operator console/SSH access limited to named Redwood operators on a per-session basis, must be pre-approved, recorded (if not prohibited by local law), and a signed attestation submitted within 48 hours. ValleyHealth observer presence required unless regulatory constraints prevent it; in those cases, an approved remote witness agent with recorded video is an alternative.

4) Costs & limits: Redwood will provide one evidence snapshot per 12-month period at no charge; additional requests billable per the Order Form rate card. We also recommend adding a clause for redaction of customer PII before delivery, with ValleyHealth sign-off.

Notes: we left placeholders for items your counsel flagged (chain-of-custody format and escrow-like wording). Baker & Co — if you have standard language that ValleyHealth prefers, please drop into the redline doc.

Alex Martinez
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redline_msa_valleyhealth.docx (docx)

From: Katie Lin <katie@valleyhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@valleyhealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, contracts@bakerco.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 13:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator access and evidence window for on-prem deployment

Naomi / Alex — this is helpful, thank you. A few clarifications from procurement and legal: 

- The 30-day non-emergency window is acceptable as-is; incident SLA 7-day turnaround is critical.
- We need the chain-of-custody manifest to include signer identity, hash values (sha256) for each artifact, and transfer method (SFTP with rotation token or witnessed USB courier for air-gapped sites).
- The 1-per-12-month complimentary snapshot is fine; procurement will request pricing for two additional snapshots per year as an optional Order Form line item.

Next steps: procurement will prepare an Order Form addendum with the pricing band and signature blocks. Baker & Co will follow up with a short paragraph on chain-of-custody standards. Can Redwood confirm you will provide the redlined Exhibit G and an operations annex (1-2 pages) by Monday 6/25 so our legal counsel can fold into the master MSA?

Best,
Katie
Attachment: procurement_terms_v2.pdf (pdf)
